scenes.tts: One evening Monod walked into the lab with his coat still on, stared at the bench, and told his colleague Agnès Ullmann, "I have discovered the second secret of life."
scenes.narration: One evening Monod walked into the lab with his coat still on, stared at the bench, and told his colleague Agnès Ullmann, "I have discovered the second secret of life."

scenes.tts: A biologist who preferred thinking to tinkering, shaping theories with a pipe while others ran the bench, he had intuited that proteins are not rigid machines but flexible structures with two kinds of site: one that does the work and one that controls whether the work can happen at all. He named the effect allostery but had no mechanism for it.

scenes.tts: The picture met its proof when he and the thermodynamicist Jeffries Wyman met over a blackboard at the Institut Pasteur in 1964: the biologist had the picture and no proof, the thermodynamicist had the proof and no picture.
